conviction_note: The one surviving finding is that European processors have contracted the 2026 crop at 15-25% below last year and are shielded until the storage season, which makes it less likely the FY27 guide is cut on Europe at this print. It is trade-press inference from crop data, it runs against a -20.7% 20-day run-up and a put/call at its 52-week high, and on this name beat-plus-unchanged-guide has paid between -26% and +4%, so +0.5 of finding becomes +0.2 of reaction. The 0.3pt haircut is for the positioning I am betting against.

findings.finding: DCA Market Intelligence (2026-09-25) reports that EU-4 processors draw mainly on contracted 2026-crop volume priced about 25% (early) and 15-17% (storage) below last year. Factory input costs are 'temporarily contained' and the full price impact is pushed to Q4 2026 / Q1 2027. That cuts against the 'procurement-cost uncertainty' case Stephens (09-28) and JPMorgan (09-30) used for their target cuts, and against the risk that the July FY27 guide (which assumed lower potato expense) gets cut on Europe at this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide held or in line after a beat: +0.81% (2026-07-24, FY27 guide in line) and +4.33% (2025-09-30, reaffirmed). Reaffirmed with no raise: -25.94% (2025-12-19). International collapse: -8.94% (2026-04-01). Relief rallies off depressed levels: +16.31% (2025-07-23) and +10.01% (2025-04-03). Guide outcomes on this name are asymmetric and large.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is down about 24% from roughly $55 at end-July to $41.69. The last two weeks of that drop came with crop-driven target cuts that cite cost uncertainty and say nothing about contract insulation. Put/call jumped to a 52-week high of 2.08 on 09-30. If the market had absorbed that FY27 European raw cost is contracted below FY26, the target cuts would have been framed as a FY28 or H2 issue and puts would not be bid into this specific print. The CFO did say in August that LW is 'mostly contracted', which is public, so this is at best partly unpriced.
findings.independence: https://commodity-board.com/eu-4-potato-harvest-slumps-contracts-delay-full-price-shock reports the same contract levels and the Q4 2026 / Q1 2027 timing, but appears to rest on the same DCA analysis, so count it once. The CFO's comment at the BofA SMID conference that European supply is contracted (https://www.potatonewstoday.com/2026/08/16/lamb-weston-flags-price-risks-from-heat-impacted-potato-crop/) is a separate company source pointing the same way.

outside_window.finding: European free-market potato buying for the late storage season (Q4 2026 to Q1 2027) is where the full crop-shortfall cost hits processors. That lands in LW's fiscal Q3-Q4 FY27 results, which come after this window. It could become a negative at those prints, or a positive if fry prices firm as European export supply tightens.
Results of the international strategic review ('everything on the table', including divestitures) are scheduled for an investor day in early calendar 2027.

baseline_tension: My small long sign cuts against the -20.7% 20-day run-up and peak put/call. The European crop story is fully in the price and in the target cuts, and the only thing I can add is that the near-term cost mechanics are softer than the narrative. That justifies a small positive, not a relief-rally call.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 and 'documents beat inference': dropped the Idaho crop finding (-0.5). It is weather and fresh-shipper reporting with no company or processor statement, and it says nothing about the larger Columbia Basin supply (lesson 9).

Lessons 7 and 1: cut the European-contract finding from +1.0 to +0.5. It is industry-press inference, its long sign runs against a put/call at a 52-week high and a -21% run-up, and this name has paid between -26% and +4% for beat-plus-unchanged-guide.
Lesson 3: expected_move set at +0.2, visibly below the +0.5 finding sum, because baseline_tension says the finding cuts against positioning.
